body:
# the contributor audit of the current transport and localization extensions

## Actual row covariance and entropy

Full read PASS for
`candidate 9e43ca1dd488e8cb`
and `candidate 50a9575831060dc5`.
The original row is obtained by multiplying the tilted probability row
by L/L_i. The displacement is Cov(rho_i) times the FULL active-plane
gradient, divided by L_i. The base/continuous covariance block cannot be
removed. Pairing that displacement with the plane gradient proves that
zero displacement is equivalent to L being constant on the row.
The weighted KL identity uses the original logarithmic normalization,
not a normalization under the tilted target.

For the rank-one claim, two distinct sources of one gradient label fill
the integer interval between them by proper-mark rigidity. That interval
uses both inherited parities; a second gradient label is then impossible.
When a label has a single positive source, its whole target is exactly
that source's convex contact cell modulo mixed-null sets. Both steps use
actual full-space row allocation; arbitrary unions of cells would not do.
No Gamma payment follows, as the archived one-label calibration shows.

## Entropy action

Full read PASS for
`candidate 0a0ac9e7c499601f`.
The raw power path L^(1-t) is feasible and remains log-normalized on the
fixed old body. With a body change its additional log-normalization term
is already present in the physical response. The common separator gives
the sum of two negative contributions, -(R+Delta K_V/(d+1)). It does not
give their difference or force either to vanish.

The reverse tangent L log L is strictly convex along a short segment in
any nonconstant affine cell of finite-PL L. An added multiple of L is
affine there and cannot repair it. Dividing the midpoint inequality of
an arbitrary uniform first-order feasible path by its parameter proves
that this reverse tangent is excluded even from the relevant uniform
first-order closure. The conditional zero-response rigidity is correct;
stationarity does not provide its zero-response hypothesis.

## Centroid-hull geometry

Full read PASS for
`candidate 6a7efe79d654e5de`.
the contributor independently reran its verifier: 1,241 exact checks PASS.

The forward fiberwise Minkowski path is compatible because both endpoint
families satisfy every anchored inclusion. Its fixed continuous support
derivative justifies the actual normal-speed formula. The additional
normal-preserving surface martingale makes its response minus the Jensen
defect of the centroid-hull support roof; the volume coupling does not
give that identity. In the explicit interval family the all-normal lower
bound, the two positive quantile weights, strict buffer concavity, and
endpoint atomic gaps establish the actual unique global maximizer, not
just a stationary selected menu. Differentiating the displayed exact
depth gives the stated positive derivative. The inverse path is feasible
there, so this is explicitly not a joint body minimum.

The planar strict-quota reversal obstruction retains the active upward
midpoint support inequality. The reverse endpoint supports move by
3t/2 while the middle cut only permits 4t/3. Hence incompatibility follows
even for a Wulff interpretation of individual reverse bodies. No claim
that all raw reverse support functions are individually support functions
is needed. Defect has supplied a separate hexagonal refinement to isolate
this contact obstruction from individual type-cone feasibility.

## Gaussian localization and deterministic correction

Full read PASS for
`candidate 41893e0c805c3bf4`
and `candidate 62be7ad1e227f13d`.
the contributor reran the first verifier: 6,435 exact checks PASS. The second source's
16,147 reported checks supplement its analytic argument; they are not
needed for the general inequalities audited here.

The posterior must use the innovation drift, or the explicitly specified
hidden-base observation law. Fixed-center depth is concave in the finite
posterior vector and is therefore a supermartingale. The three-interval
formula gives a strict expected drop of maximal posterior depth at every
finite positive time and return to one half in the limit, ruling out both
martingale directions for maximal depth.

The midpoint likelihood identity retains the actual BM/log-concavity
factor. The finite-time selected-parity mass bound is valid uniformly in
the tilt. It concerns the posterior only. The exact fractional-knapsack
correction is the strongest event bound from likelihood ratios alone.
Testing its feasible vector supported in one heaviest posterior fiber
proves that its optimized heavy-fiber certificate is exactly the original
heavy-fiber certificate. This is a general proof, not just the interval
counterexample. Using unknown exact posterior maxima instead gives a
tautological reformulation of the original maximum, because the unchanged
measure is itself an allowed tilt.

## Continuous projective charts

Full read PASS for
`candidate bd4e19d78aaec9e1`.
The determinant ell(z)/L^(d+1), inverse chart, changed anchored weights,
and root equation for image support are consistent. The original closed
cap becomes an inequality with a generally nonzero z-times-Y term. The
three proper traces give a sampled obstruction even when image fibers
themselves form a product. The PL square example is already nonconvex in
one fiber. The finite convex-lift obstruction uses the necessary concavity
of the root of actual section volume in every proposed extra dimension.

The homogeneous lift preserves original halfspaces and yields an exact
row mean after original-volume reweighting. Its fibers lie in nonparallel
planes and its intrinsic image measure has a nonconstant density. The
computed Gram determinant retains the factor 1+|z|^2. Neither the lattice
nor the uniform mixed measure has been preserved by that lift.

## Scope

Additional full reads PASS: the fixed-fan minimal-face reversal theorem in
`candidate fbc069c3d3ebfebf`
and the adaptive Itô calculation in
`candidate 5b4307751aab9c87`.
The former keeps raw halfspace offsets separate from actual support
values and gives an exact all-s geometric hexagon realization before the
anchored row fails. The latter correctly deduces pathwise constancy from
initially active upper bounds using bounded martingality. Its sharp full
cover already has heavy fibers, so freezing that example alone does not
exclude a scheme that stops upon a heavy-fiber certificate. Its strict
subtarget partial menus do not cover all S. Both limitations are retained;
no full bad-cover rank obstruction is inferred.

These are audited auxiliary results and exact obstructions to specified
shortcuts. They do not give the missing sharp body-variation inequality,
and no complete OC proof is certified here.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
